title: The Perfect Autopsy
premise: Cyrus Reyes, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made her the person detectives call when a death doesn't add up, is summoned to examine the body of a woman found wearing clothes stolen from Cyrus's own closet — down to a monogrammed scarf she lost years ago. As she reconstructs the victim's life, she realizes the killer isn't just mimicking her: he's staging deaths from old case files she personally closed, each one an 'imperfect autopsy' she signed off on, forcing her to relitigate her own judgments. The killer turns out to be Daniel Voss, the brother of a man whose wrongful death Cyrus helped bury in a settlement a decade ago — a man who now works inside the medical examiner's office and uses his access to weaponize her own reports against her. In the final act, Cyrus lets Voss stage one last 'perfect autopsy' using her as the intended subject, feeding him false file details through a leaked decoy report; when he comes to complete the tableau, she traps him with recorded confession and physical evidence of his tampering, choosing to hand him to justice rather than become it — though the epilogue hints the institution that enabled him will never face its own reckoning.
about_author: Noor Brightwater spent eleven years as a claims adjuster in the Pacific Northwest before turning to fiction, drawing on a caseload of strange deaths and stranger survivors. She writes mysteries about ordinary people who discover that paperwork can be more violent than any knife.

chapters.title: The Wrong Coat
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Called to a riverside crime scene, Cyrus recognizes the dead woman's coat — hers, reported stolen two winters ago — and feels the case tilt from professional to personal. The detective on scene, Marisol Quade, wants her read on the body. Emotional beat: cold dread disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Photographs of Everything
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Flashback-tinged chapter establishing Cyrus's photographic memory and her reputation for closing 'unresolvable' claims. She reviews her mental snapshot of the scene and notices details no one photographed: the victim's shoes are laced wrong, like a re-enactment by someone who only saw photos. Beat: unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: File 4471
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Digging through archives, Cyrus matches the staging to a drowning claim she closed eight years ago — one she ruled accidental against her own instinct because the payout was cheaper than the fight. Beat: guilt surfacing under procedural calm.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: POV alternating Cyrus/Quade. A second victim appears, staged from another Reyes-closed file, this time wearing Cyrus's watch. The press sniffs a serial pattern; the department resents the outsider. Beat: the hunt becomes public, and Cyrus becomes suspect-adjacent.

chapters.title: What the ME Missed
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. At the morgue, assistant examiner Daniel Voss is helpful, precise, oddly familiar with her old reports — quoting phrasing only the author would know. Cyrus's memory flags his voice from a decade-old deposition. Beat: first brush with the killer without knowing it.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Her old supervisor warns her off reopening settled claims: the company's liability window is closing, and someone upstairs wants the past buried. Cyrus realizes the killer may be counting down to a legal deadline, not just taunting her. Beat: institutional pressure versus conscience.

chapters.title: The Brother
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. She tracks the family behind File 4471 and finds Daniel Voss changed his name after his brother's death — the brother whose autopsy she helped make 'inconclusive.' Beat: vertigo; the case was always about her.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Memory
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus, intimate and interior. Unable to sleep, Cyrus mentally replays every case she closed wrong, building a list of candidates the killer might stage next. She confides in Quade, trading credibility for alliance. Beat: vulnerability as strategy.

chapters.title: Third Staging
chapters.summary: POV Quade. A third body, dressed in Cyrus's late mother's clothing — items never photographed, meaning the killer had access somewhere deeper than files. Suspicion inside the department turns toward Cyrus herself. Beat: paranoia closing in from all sides.

chapters.title: Suspended
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. The insurer suspends her, and Quade is ordered to treat her as a person of interest. Stripped of official access, Cyrus goes off-book, using her memory instead of credentials. Beat: exile; justice must now happen outside the law.

chapters.title: The Copyist's Signature
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Comparing the three scenes in her head, Cyrus isolates a repeated error — a detail altered identically each time, a fingerprint of imitation. Whoever stages these bodies learned death from documents, not from killing. Beat: the profile crystallizes.

chapters.title: Night Shift at the Morgue
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. She breaks into the ME's office after hours and finds Voss's private archive: annotated copies of every Reyes report, corrections in red, a ledger grading her autopsies like a teacher grading essays. Beat: horror mixed with terrible admiration.

chapters.title: Confrontation, Deferred
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus/Voss. Voss catches her in the archive but doesn't call security; instead he speaks obliquely about his brother and 'people who sign their names to lies.' He lets her leave, which frightens her more than arrest would. Beat: the trap is mutual now.

chapters.title: What I Signed
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. She revisits her brother-of-the-victim file and admits what she always knew: the death was homicide, and she buried it for a settlement. She drafts a confession of her own complicity. Beat: moral nadir; identity as the thing corrupted.

chapters.title: Quade's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Quade. Quade finds Cyrus's unauthorized break-in evidence and must decide: arrest her or work with her. She chooses Cyrus, burning her own career bridge, and they build an off-the-books plan. Beat: loyalty forged in shared transgression.

chapters.title: The Decoy File
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. They plant a falsified 'final' Reyes report where Voss will find it — a staged fifth case with Cyrus listed as next subject, details subtly wrong. Only the real killer would correct them. Beat: turning defense into bait.

chapters.title: Corrections in Red
chapters.summary: POV Voss (first killer POV). Voss finds the decoy and cannot resist annotating it, correcting Cyrus's 'errors' with loving precision — including the time and place he intends to finish the tableau. Beat: intimacy of obsession; the reader sees his logic whole.

chapters.title: The Perfect Autopsy
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. In the decommissioned lab where his brother died, Voss prepares to stage Cyrus's death as the flawless version of every botched file. She talks to him as the investigator he's always wanted — the only witness who truly reads his work. Beat: climax begins; power inverted.

chapters.title: Every Detail Correct
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus/Quade. Cyrus springs the trap: the room is wired, Quade close, and Voss's own corrected annotations — his handwriting, his access logs, his recorded confession — assemble into an airtight case. He nearly kills her anyway; she survives by knowing him better than he knows himself. Beat: climax resolved by memory, not force.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Voss is charged, but prosecutors balk at tainted evidence; Cyrus testifies, submitting her own decade-old complicity into the record alongside his crimes. Justice arrives impure but real. Beat: cost acknowledged.

chapters.title: Reopening
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. With Voss convicted, Cyrus formally reopens every file he used, reversing her old rulings and sending restitution to the families — starting with Voss's brother's, delivered to a mother who spits at her name. Beat: justice outside the law still demands payment.

chapters.title: The Empty Closet
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Epilogue: Cyrus returns the recovered clothes to her closet, keeps one hanger empty for the woman who died in her coat, and resigns from the insurer to consult independently for families the system failed. Final image: a new case file on her desk, unopened. Beat: quiet, earned resolve.
